Exact source changes:
1. src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp
   - detach_extent rejects physical && maybe_attached && !attached before any
     unmap/drain/destroy. It poisons and reports that teardown is required.
   - map_extras returns the original attach failure immediately for an unknown
     failed extent, before rollback drain/unmap. It retains all prior successful
     maps, the failed physical handle, reservation and backend/context ownership.
   - close scans all extents for unknown state before quiescence or cleanup.
     Repeated close returns failure without unmap/destroy/release or callbacks.
     A failed detach still sets attached=false and leaves maybe_attached=true;
     the next close therefore cannot retry it or clean up another extent first.
   - The existing destructor's std::terminate when base_ is retained is unchanged.
2. include/strata/core/phase_cache_owner.hpp
   - Backend comments no longer suggest unsuccessful operations are atomic.
   - close contract explicitly states retained physical/virtual/backend ownership
     and no unknown-state recovery; known-unmapped release-failure retry remains.
3. tests/core/phase_cache_owner_test.cpp
   - Added mock detach/release attempt counters and two synthetic possible
     post-error states: map failure may leave mapped or unmapped; failed unmap
     may likewise leave mapped or unmapped. Neither is a provider assertion.
   - Kept physical-creation failure rollback at both extra indices with unchanged
     exact base-only retained-byte checks and ordinary checked cleanup.
   - Replaced invalid repair-and-close unknown-state cleanup with 11 Linux fork
     subprocess cases: six unknown attach cases (base, first extra, second extra,
     each mapped/unmapped); two extra-detach cases; one rollback-detach case;
     two close-detach cases. Heap owners survive until child _exit without
     owner/backend destructors. Parent requires normal exit status zero.
   - Each child checks original failing return/state (and native attach/detach
     error where appropriate), retained handles/bytes/reservation, poisoned
     request rejection, no readers, and three failing closes after clearing
     synthetic faults. No later unmap/free/destroy attempts or callbacks allowed.
   - Attach cases require exact 2/4/6-MiB retained counts, zero rollback unmap or
     destroy/free attempts, failed extent uncertain, and backend weak_ptr still
     alive after external shared ownership is reset. Extra attach failures begin
     from a published baseline to verify readers become inaccessible afterward.
   - Kept ordinary success/geometry/pre-map/write/read/corrupt/drain/release,
     quota, orchestration and pending-D2H safety fixtures and their count checks.
     Non-Linux explicitly prints a subprocess coverage skip; W supports Linux.
4. docs/PHASE_DECODE_CACHE.ja.md then docs/PHASE_DECODE_CACHE.md
   - Japanese first, matching English: unknown map/unmap state retains ownership
     until teardown; repeated close has no recovery; subprocess fixtures and
     synthetic/provider evidence limits are described.

Successful paths and limits:
No successful-path math, quota, flags, source/timing implementation or counters
were changed. Native map/unmap timing calls remain around actual attempts.
New close failures still contribute failed close timing via the existing timer;
rejected cleanup never fabricates unmap/destroy/release timing attempts.
Known physical-allocation failures may rollback prior confirmed mapped extents.
Unknown attach stops immediately; no attempt is made to reclaim even earlier
successful mappings. A first failed unmap stops that operation; future close
globally rejects cleanup. This deliberately retains memory until process exit.
There is no test-only production escape hatch, no provider atomicity assumption,
no direct Level Zero recovery, no SDK map-fault GPU test, and no recovery query.
This fixes portable owner decisions; it neither establishes actual provider
post-error behavior nor claims an observed production UB or GPU qualification.
